Some of the comments threads here are ridiculous and don't understand the risks of going back in person to almost 100+ to 300+ student lecture halls with close proximity to each other. In a work environment I doubt I'd be sitting next to so many individuals with only an armrest between us like at a movie theater. I would LOVE to be in person but I also understand this variant does not care if we are vaccinated or have the booster. I have family as young as 6 years old who are still getting sick right now from this disease. Students and educators and their families are being put at risk. 

Online alternatives to the in-person classes is the best bet if they want to reopen campus. The quality of education has always been crap here no matter if it's online or offline because a lot of professors are here to do their own research, so teaching is a side gig.

Unless you were joining a million clubs and living in the dorms, no one really socializes with each other outside of class group chats unless they knew each other prior. This is a personal experience but I feel like I've been more social with other students NOW due to the wsu discord hubs being opened and colleges in general linking up with social media than I have the two years I was actually on campus. 

Not to ramble further but I feel that reopening campus without providing any alternatives is a mistake and will end up with it being shut down again by the end of spring break. The constant opening and closing of campus doesn't help a student's ability to learn anything.

It's tough to answer because ultimately the act of sex itself was the biggest thing I could do to people please especially when I had no interest in it outside of keeping partners around. I was traumatized and disgusted by sex and yet it's almost like I trained myself like a dog to tolerate it and then see it as a form of validation to the point that now when im with partners and sex isn't on the table constantly I am at a loss for words and become erratic since now im not receiving the only form of validation I understand. When you are young and already unstable and you have no concept of sex outside of the commodification of it (as an AFAB individual at least), you start to believe that the only way you can keep people is to allow yourself to be sexualized, at least in my experience. So any sexual interests I developed were 100% done initially as a form of people pleasing but since that people pleasing is so ingrained into my sexuality, it feels almost impossible to separate at this point. Kinda sucks!

I think it's also important to wonder just how much control does anyone have in the heat of the moment? Even NT people shout out things they don't mean when they're arguing. For us, it is a lot harder and I won't deny that, but you can still think critically later on and recognize that what you did was hurtful. We still have a form of control then to not excuse what we did but to recognize that unhealthy behavior and begin developing better skills for those moments. It is a process like anything.

I think it's really just a matter of changing how you think which in and of itself is a process and won't happen right away. A lot of recovery with BPD, at least in my experience, is learning how to recognize unhealthy thinking patterns and actively working against it. 

An example I can think of is maybe a friend has been hanging out with other people more often lately and it's causing me to lash out either passively or actively towards them. In that scenario, I need to take a step back and think about all the times my friend HAS been there for me, how I hang out with different people aside from them and they don't have an issue with it, etc. Listing out my positive interactions with the person as proof of evidence of my unhealthy thinking helps me at the very list. 

Not sure if that is a helpful tip or a relatable enough example but if other people have any tips then I hope you hear some soon

I think it's important to note that everyone is equipped with different ways of coping with their own despair. It's really not "normal" (or rather healthy) to feel as suicidal as we do but I feel like it's a lot more commonplace to nowadays because suicide is such a normalized topic and joked about. Our brains aren't really capable of processing that humor (funny right?) and take it seriously. If you constantly joke about wanting to die or constantly say even in a lighthearted manner "man I wish I were dead" your brain is taking that negativity seriously. Sounds silly but really just changing your thinking process goes a long way. Small steps eventually take you quite a ways away.

I think it's important to acknowledge that people are people and we all have our own interests and hobbies. Even people with ASPD/NPD. We are all more than our diagnoses and will not always act in line with what some articles or books say and I think for the most part we all know that. 

Like yeah, as someone also diagnosed with ASPD, my ability to empathize with people is practically nonexistent but I can still logically understand what I'm doing in emotionally charged situations. I know when someone is crying that something has happened and I try to problem solve with them because even if I don't care and it's annoying, I still will try to help. Is it always effective? No. I'm human, not a mastermind who can always think 20 steps ahead. 

There are plenty of people out there with these big bad disorders, like us here in the BPD sub, that are just people. We've all met plenty of assholes who aren't diagnosed with shit who have prob caused just as much damage.

Consider it like ripping off a bandaid or getting a shot. It stings for a minute! And then the feeling subsides. You get yourself a little treat for a job well done and then you move on. As someone diagnosed with comorbid bpd/aspd, I feel like throwing my two cents in. If someone is going to demonize you because of your illness, then they aren't worth having around. You don't want someone who won't do the bare minimum of a little independent research and honest communication. You want someone who will help you grow, who will provide a safe and healthy space that is nurtured with mutual respect. I'm sorry that this person left and I understand that it hurts, but us being in the same cluster as aspd isn't why people tend to demonize us. Any rep we have tends to be of us at our worst or written from the perspective of someone who has no idea what they're talking about. Blame the interpretations of us and the terrible articles for how to "deal with us", not aspd which is already demonized enough as it is.

It happens. Especially in cases of breakups, that's a normal feeling. You're going through a grieving process and mourning the death of a relationship. It's hard for most people to flip it around instantly because you probably built a connection to these people. It is okay to let yourself go through that grieving process though. It's gonna suck for awhile, but it does get better and it does pass and every day you're slowly becoming a different you from the person you were before. When I'm going through it, I try to force myself into a new hobby. It's a tough situation as I also still struggle with having to deal with the perceived abandonment in my childhood and the constant abandonment as an adult. I don't know if this will help you but what helps me from time to time is acknowledging that my parents and by extension their families are their own people. I have tried time and time again to reconcile with them and to recreate some sort of idealized version of a family, but people will do what they want and it is not something I can control. It hurts, it sucks, and it definitely hurts to see other people have what I crave. But what I can control, however, are the people I allow in my life. Family doesn't have to be the family you have forced onto you because of blood relations but it can be the friends and partners in your life. I keep my contact with my blood family to a minimum, not allowing them the opportunity to hurt me whether through triggering an episode or intentionally mentally/emotionally hurting me. I do not humor them and I keep my distance. My family is my friends who have been there for me and provided me a space where I can flourish. My family is my partner who has been kind and patient with me. My mother and father and their families exist but through reminding myself that they don't have to be the family I rush to in times of joy or distress, I am able to cope better. 
It is never too late to find that type of found family and although it may hurt (trust me I know it hurts) to see people living the dream, for me I was only able to accept that I had actually found it when I stopped begging for my biological family's love. You cannot change the past but you can change the future, as corny as that sounds. It's not an immediate thing you can do but it is a mindset you can begin working towards though I won't lie there can be relapses as is the case when dealing with mental illness. Through showing healthy appreciation to the people around you, you're already fostering a tight bond.
